title: Induction by stages: G ×^P̃(G' ×^P' X'') ≅ G ×^P X''
body_html:
Induction by stages

Let $G'' \le G' \le G$, and suppose $P$ is a cosheaf of subgroups of $G$ on a $G''$-space $X''$ satisfying (P1)–(P2) for the pair $G'' \le G$. Define

$$ P'_E := P_E \cap G' \qquad (E \in X''), $$

a cosheaf of subgroups of $G'$ on $X''$ (satisfying (P1)–(P2) for $G'' \le G'$). Let $X' := G' \times^{P'} X''$ be the intermediate induced $G'$-space, and extend $P$ to $X'$ by

$$ \widetilde P_{[(g', E)]} \;:=\; g' P_E (g')^{-1}; $$

well-definedness on $\sim$-classes uses (P1) for $P$: for $(g'1, E_1) \sim{P'} (g'2, E_2)$ via witness $n \in G''$ with $n \cdot E_1 = E_2$ and $(g'_1)^{-1} g'_2 n \in P'{E_1} \subseteq P_{E_1}$, direct calculation with (P1) shows $g'1 P{E_1} (g'1)^{-1} = g'_2 P{E_2} (g'_2)^{-1}$.

The extended data $(G', \widetilde P)$ on $X'$ then satisfy (P1)–(P2) for the pair $G' \le G$, and $G \times^{\widetilde P} X'$ is the outer induced $G$-space.

Statement

Proposition (induction by stages). There is a canonical $G$-equivariant bijection $$ \Phi : G \times^{\widetilde P} \bigl(G' \times^{P'} X''\bigr) \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; G \times^P X'', \qquad \Phi\bigl([(g,\, [(g', E)])]\bigr) = [(g g',\, E)]. $$
proof_html:
via the universal property

Both sides represent the same functor $Y \mapsto \mathrm{Map}_{G'', P}(X'', Y)$ on $G$-sets $Y$, so their representing objects are canonically isomorphic.

Concretely, three applications of the universal property (Universal property of G ×^P X') chain together:

$$ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{Map}_G\Bigl(G \times^{\widetilde P}\bigl(G' \times^{P'} X''\bigr),\, Y\Bigr) &\;\underset{\text{UP outer}}{\cong}\; \mathrm{Map}_{G', \widetilde P}\bigl(G' \times^{P'} X'',\, Y\bigr) \\ &\;\underset{\text{UP inner}}{\cong}\; \mathrm{Map}_{G'', P}(X'',\, Y) \\ &\;\underset{\text{UP direct}}{\cong}\; \mathrm{Map}_G\bigl(G \times^P X'',\, Y\bigr). \end{aligned} $$

Reading off the identification on classes:

  • UP outer sends $\Psi \in \mathrm{Map}G(G \times^{\widetilde P} (G' \times^{P'} X''), Y)$ to its restriction along the outer $\iota{\text{outer}} : G' \times^{P'} X'' \hookrightarrow G \times^{\widetilde P}(G' \times^{P'} X'')$.
  • UP inner sends the resulting $G'$-map $G' \times^{P'} X'' \to Y$ to its restriction along the inner $\iota_{\text{inner}} : X'' \hookrightarrow G' \times^{P'} X''$; this restriction is a $(G'', P)$-compatible map (the $P$-fix condition and $G''$-eq. are built into the definition of $P'$ and the inner induction).
  • UP direct sends a $(G'', P)$-compatible map to its extension to a $G$-equivariant map $G \times^P X'' \to Y$.

Compose the three bijections: the resulting bijection $\mathrm{Map}_G(\text{outer}, Y) \cong \mathrm{Map}_G(\text{direct}, Y)$ is natural in $Y$, so by Yoneda / representability the two $G$-sets are canonically isomorphic. Tracing the identity on the direct side back through the three UPs recovers the class-level formula $\Phi([(g, [(g', E)])]) = [(g g', E)]$. $\square$

Consequence

The isomorphism $\Phi$ has an explicit inverse $\Phi^{-1}([(h, E)]) = [(h, [(1, E)])]$ for $h \in G$, $E \in X''$; this is the unique $G$-equivariant map factoring the composition $X'' \hookrightarrow G' \times^{P'} X'' \hookrightarrow G \times^{\widetilde P}(G' \times^{P'} X'')$ through $G \times^P X''$.

Downstream

The stages identity is exactly what extends the generalised-building cosheaf $K$ from an apartment $A$ to the full Bruhat–Tits building of $G'$; see Generalized building B(Σ) = G ×^K A. Without the universal-property route, the paper's original proof would require a class-level combinatorial calculation on the double quotient $(G \times G' \times X'')/(\sim, \sim)$; with UP, that calculation is not needed — only the routine verification that both sides represent the same $\mathrm{Map}_{G'', P}(X'', -)$ functor.

Lean formalization

The Lean formalisation of stages is not yet in place. The strategy via universalProperty (from Universal property of G ×^P X') is:

  1. Set up three InductionDatums that share the same ambient group $G$:
  2. d_inner : InductionDatum X'' with d_inner.G' = G'' (subgroup of $G$).
  3. d_outer : InductionDatum (InducedSpace d_inner) with d_outer.G' = G' and cosheaf $\widetilde P_{[(g', E)]} := g' P_E (g')^{-1}$ on InducedSpace d_inner. Its (P0)–(P2) hypotheses follow from the corresponding hypotheses of d_inner by direct calculation on representatives; the well-definedness of $\widetilde P$ on $\sim$-classes uses (P1) of d_inner.

  4. d_direct : InductionDatum X'' with d_direct.G' = G' and cosheaf $P$.

  5. Instantiate universalProperty for each side at the same target $G$-set $Y$; compose the three resulting Equivs.

  6. The resulting natural bijection $\mathrm{Map}_G(\text{outer}, Y) \cong \mathrm{Map}_G(\text{direct}, Y)$ produces the iso by applying it to $Y := \text{InducedSpace}\, d_\text{direct}$ with the identity MulActionHom, and vice versa.

Constructing d_outer is the only non-trivial piece — the routine Lean bookkeeping of verifying (P0)–(P2) for $\widetilde P$ using those of d_inner. With universalProperty already in place, the iso itself is a short composition of Equivs once d_outer is defined; no combinatorial class-level calculation $[(g, [(g', E)])] \mapsto [(g g', E)]$ is needed.

Hypotheses used

Step Datum hypotheses consumed
$\widetilde P$ well-defined on $\sim_{P'}$-classes (P1) of $P$ (equivariance)
$(G', \widetilde P)$ satisfies (P1) (P1) of $P$
$(G', \widetilde P)$ satisfies (P2) (P2) of $P$ + Yoneda-side identity computation
Three applications of universalProperty (P1) of each datum (see Universal property of G ×^P X')
Compose $\Phi$ none — pure Equiv.trans

The formula on classes $\Phi([(g, [(g', E)])]) = [(g g', E)]$ is not part of the proof — it is the transported value of the identity along the composite Equiv.
